summary: W. Pachow is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Indology who studied under Yunshan Tan. He held a teaching and research staff post at Visva-Bharati University.

W. Randolph Kloetzli is an Indology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Chicago in 1964 under multiple teachers. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai Lun Tam works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and served as professor and Department Chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris (under Paul Demiéville). He was Vice-Chancellor at University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and held posts at Northwestern and Oxford.

Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. Educated at Göttingen (~1926–1930), he held posts at SOAS/University of London (~1936–1962), Columbia (~1946–1947), and UC Berkeley (~1962–1967).

Walter Elliot (1803–1887) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at East India Company College and the College of Fort St George, later serving as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837–1842).

Walter Eugene Clark (1881–1960) was an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Harvard and under Richard Pischel. He served as assistant and associate professor at the University of Chicago and as Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).

Walter Liebenthal (1886–1982) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his doctorate at Breslau. He held academic posts at Yenching, Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Tübingen (1965–1982).

Walter M. Spink (1928–2019) was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and Harvard University (PhD) and served on the faculty at Brandeis University (1956–1961) and the University of Michigan (~1961–2000).

Walter Nowick (1926–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Juilliard and trained under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965. He held a post at Kyoto Women's University and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Porzig (1895–1961) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jena and under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held academic posts at Leipzig University, University of Bern, University of Jena, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Walter Ruben (1899–1982) was an Indology scholar. He held academic appointments at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1927–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1949), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon (1893–1981) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics educated at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin, SOAS, and the University of London, serving as Professor of Chinese from 1947 to 1960.

Walter Slaje (born 1954) is an Indologist who completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library and held a professorship at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2019.

Walter William Skeat (1835–1912) was a linguist educated at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from ~1878 until 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz (1878–1965) was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford University, the University of Oxford (Jesus College), and under Kazi Dawa Samdup from ~1919 to 1922.

Walther Heissig (1913–2005) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetan studies, earning degrees at Vienna and Göttingen. He taught at Fu Jen and Peking University, later holding the Chair of the Central Asian seminar at Bonn from 1964.

Walther Schubring (1881–1969) was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann and earned his doctorate at Strasbourg. He worked at the Berlin State Library and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg from 1920 to 1951.

Walther Wüst (1901–1993) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich as professor and Dean, led a section at Ahnenerbe, and served as president of Deutsche Akademie.
